    h=len(inp); w=len(inp[0])
    vals={}
    for r in inp:
        for v in r: vals[v]=vals.get(v,0)+1
    bg=max(vals,key=vals.get)
    fg=[c for c in vals if c!=bg][0]
    out=[row[:] for row in inp]
    for i,r in enumerate(out):
        cs=[j for j,x in enumerate(r) if x==fg]
        if len(cs)<2: continue
        p=cs[1]-cs[0]
        ok=all((j-cs[0])%p==0 for j in cs)
        if not ok: continue
        end=cs[-1]+p-1 if abs(cs[-1]+p-1-w)>abs(w-(cs[0])) else cs[-1]
        # decide end: if row has fewer than ceil(W/p) markers? Use demo heuristic: extend one more period if there's room? 
        # demo: row14 cs=[0,2] p=2 -> end=3 (one extra). row1 cs=[5..15] p=2 -> end=15 (no extra).
        # heuristic: extend by one period if cs[-1]+p < w-? row1 cs[-1]=15,p=2,w=26: 17<26 but no extension.
        # difference: row14's first marker near left edge. Extension happens when pattern starts near edge? 
        # row10 cs=[1..17] p=2 -> end=17 no extra though.
        # maybe rule: fill [cs[0], cs[-1]] always, PLUS if cs[0]==0? row14 cs[0]=0 -> extra at 3.
        # check others with cs[0]!=0: none extra. Good enough: extend if cs[0]==0 and room? risky.
        rng=(cs[-1],end) if end>cs[-1] else (cs[0],cs[-1])
        for j in range(rng[0],rng[1]+1):
